title: Change: Why the right choice is almost always to change, and how to manage it kindly
summary: Jason Cohen argues that everyone wants change but nobody wants to change, yet the right choice is almost always to change because it reflects new facts or a shifting environment. Leaders must recognize that change is exhausting, watch for burnout, and manage it with kindness while still holding organizations accountable for striving to improve.

principles.text: The right choice is almost always to change, since change responds to new facts, learning, or environment shifts.
principles.quote: **The right choice is almost always "change."** This is because change is a reaction to uncovering facts, getting smarter, or a shift in the external environment.

principles.text: Organizations that prefer the comfort of the familiar over the discomfort of change die.
principles.quote: Death awaits any organization that chooses the comfort of the familiar over the discomfort of change.

principles.text: Strategy that never changes despite new information is wrong, but constant flux makes strategy ineffective too.
principles.quote: [Strategy](https://longform.asmartbear.com/great-strategy/) is ineffective if it's constantly in flux, but a strategy that remains unchanged in the presence of new information is incorrect.

principles.text: Even change-loving people need breaks; leaders should watch for burnout and decision-fatigue and address it proactively.
principles.quote: Even your most stoic, change-loving mortals sometimes need a break from change.

principles.text: Distinguish a rudderless company from a culture of self-reflection, since constant change can feel like no plan.
principles.quote: Constant change can feel like management has no plan and no strategy. It takes careful consideration to distinguish between being rudderless and a culture of self-reflection and improvement.

principles.text: What got you here won't necessarily get you there; success can stall from losing core insights or from dogmatism when the world or scale changes.
principles.quote: It is not generally true that "what got us here will get us there," and that means deep change is required.
